title: Ensemble Learning
text: Ensemble learning combines the predictions of multiple machine learning models to produce a final prediction that is often more accurate and robust than any single model alone. Bagging methods, such as random forests, train models independently on different subsets of the data and combine their outputs by averaging or voting. Boosting methods, such as gradient boosting, train models sequentially, where each new model focuses on correcting the errors made by the previous ones.

title: Feature Engineering
text: Feature engineering is the process of transforming raw data into features that better represent the underlying problem to a machine learning model. Good features can make a simple model perform well, while poor features can make even a powerful model fail. Common feature engineering techniques include scaling numerical values, encoding categorical variables, and creating new features by combining existing ones. Domain knowledge often plays a large role in designing effective features.

title: Train-Test Split
text: A train-test split divides a dataset into a portion used to train a machine learning model and a separate portion used to evaluate it. The test set must never be used during training, otherwise the evaluation will be overly optimistic and will not reflect real-world performance. A common practice is to also hold out a validation set, distinct from the test set, used for tuning hyperparameters. Splitting data correctly, before any preprocessing that looks at the whole dataset, is essential to avoid data leakage.

title: Reinforcement Learning
text: Reinforcement learning is a branch of machine learning where an agent learns to make decisions by interacting with an environment. The agent takes actions, observes the resulting state of the environment, and receives a reward signal that tells it how good or bad the action was. Over many interactions, the agent learns a policy that maximizes cumulative reward. Reinforcement learning is commonly used in robotics, game playing, and resource management.

title: Embeddings
text: An embedding is a learned, dense vector representation of a discrete object such as a word, so that objects with similar meaning or usage end up close together in the vector space. Embeddings are typically learned by training a model on a task where nearby context predicts useful structure, such as predicting a word from its surrounding words. Once learned, embeddings can be reused as input features for other machine learning models, and distances between embedding vectors often reflect meaningful semantic relationships.
